mechanism_narrative: Sustained recovery in WORKPLACES mobility over the next four weeks will drive commuter-adjacent retail visits. The current -21.0% workplace deficit will narrow as restrictions ease, pulling RETAIL_REC upward through increased weekday foot traffic.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined from -14.3% (t-3w) to -39.9% (t-1w) then recovered to -21.0% (t-0w)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than the preceding 28-day mean, or WORKPLACES fails to improve by at least 5 percentage points within the first two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility volatility (ranging from -29.3% to +6.0% across four weeks) signals shifting outdoor preference. When PARKS rises above -10%, consumers redirect discretionary spending from home-based activities to retail venues, increasing RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -10% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS recovered to +6.0% at t-1w before falling to -32.1% at t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS remains below -15% for three consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines despite PARKS exceeding -10%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station usage and RETAIL_REC are jointly constrained by capacity restrictions. When TRANSIT falls below -45%, retail venues operate under severe occupancy caps. Recovery of TRANSIT above -40% signals policy relaxation, enabling retail reopening and higher RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 8 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: TRANSIT remains below -42% for four consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines despite TRANSIT improvement exceeding 8 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM volatility (-10.1% to +2.4%) reflects essential-goods demand stability. When GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes above -5%, it signals consumer confidence in public spaces, enabling discretionary retail visits and lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -5% and remains stable for one week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at t-0w is -3.6%, above the t-1w low of -10.1%
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -8% within the first week, or RETAIL_REC declines in the first week despite GROCERY_PHARM stability above -5%.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL elevation (6.3% at t-0w) combined with RETAIL_REC depression (-15.1%) indicates suppressed demand, not supply constraint. As RESIDENTIAL normalizes toward baseline over four weeks, pent-up retail demand will release, driving RETAIL_REC upward.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines toward 0% over two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL remains above 5% for all four weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to improve despite RESIDENTIAL declining toward baseline.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-April timing in Madrid coincides with spring reopening cycles. PARKS volatility and TRANSIT recovery signal seasonal mobility shifts. Interaction of improving PARKS (+6.0% at t-1w) and stabilizing TRANSIT (-41.4% at t-0w) will jointly lift RETAIL_REC as outdoor-to-retail substitution occurs.
candidate_trigger: PARKS positive and TRANSIT improves by >5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached +6.0% at t-1w; TRANSIT improved from -47.0% to -41.4%
failure_condition: PARKS returns to negative territory for two consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines despite both PARKS and TRANSIT improving simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and RETAIL_REC are coupled through commuter-driven foot traffic. The sharp t-1w decline in WORKPLACES (-39.9%) preceded t-0w RETAIL_REC depression (-15.1%). Reversal of the WORKPLACES shock over the next two weeks will restore retail traffic.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by more than 10 percentage points from t-0w baseline
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES collapsed from -13.7% (t-2w) to -39.9% (t-1w), recovering partially to -21.0% (t-0w)
failure_condition: WORKPLACES fails to improve by 10 percentage points within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines despite WORKPLACES recovery exceeding 10 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and GROCERY_PHARM jointly indicate policy regime. When both stabilize above their respective -40% and -5% thresholds, it signals sustained reopening policy. This dual-signal regime enables RETAIL_REC recovery over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT above -40% AND GROCERY_PHARM above -5% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at t-0w is -41.4%; GROCERY_PHARM at t-0w is -3.6%
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT falls below -42% or GROCERY_PHARM falls below -8% for two consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines despite both proxies meeting trigger thresholds.
